title: Solara Tech - POC capacity & autoscale scoping
summary: Redwood AE + SE scoped a POC for Solara Tech focused on capacity sizing and autoscaling. Discussed baseline workload, target latency and cost success criteria, reserved GPU pool size, burst strategy using spot instances, and fallback policies to smaller quantized models or hosted endpoints. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send capacity/pricing proposal, run a short benchmark with Solara sample workload, and share security docs. Timeline target: pilot in 2-3 weeks, production decision by end of Q1.
next_steps: Maya to send capacity and pricing proposal with reserved + burst options by 2025-12-05
Solara to provide 24-48 hour sample traffic trace and 50 representative prompts by 2025-12-08
Diego to schedule a 2-hour benchmark run with Solara and run p95 latency + throughput tests (week of 2025-12-08)
Maya to share security docs (SOC2, data retention, KMS integrations) and draft SSO plan
Schedule follow-up to review benchmark results and finalize pilot SLOs on 2025-12-15
action_items: Maya Chen - send capacity/pricing proposal (reserved GPUs + burst strategy) - due 2025-12-05
Diego Ramirez - run benchmark with sample workload, collect p50/p95/p99 and costs - due 2025-12-12
Anika Patel - provide sample traffic trace and representative prompts - due 2025-12-08
Priya Singh - confirm VPC and KMS requirements and provide security contact - due 2025-12-09
meeting_header:
Date: 2025-12-03 14:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramirez (Redwood SE), Anika Patel (Solara Head of ML), Liam O'Neal (Solara Platform Eng), Priya Singh (Solara SRE)
Recording: yes
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i think we have about an hour, uh Diego and i will run through the POC scope for capacity and autoscale.
[00:12] Anika Patel: cool, thanks, quick note we're on a tight timeline, goal to have a pilot running in a couple weeks, decision by end of Q1.
[00:20] Diego Ramirez: understood. can you walk us through current traffic and workloads? like average rps, peak, typical sequence lengths.
[00:28] Liam O'Neal: yeah so baseline is about 80 rps on our chat endpoints during business hours, peaks can hit ~250 for dips around launches. seq lengths are 64 tokens avg, but some flows go up to 800 for long-form summarization.
[00:42] Priya Singh: most inference is user-facing so p95 latency matters, we're targeting sub 200ms p95 if possible.
[00:50] Maya Chen: good, that's helpful. for a POC we usually propose a small reserved pool plus burst capacity. Diego, quick sketch on sizing?
[01:00] Diego Ramirez: sure. given 80 rps steady with 250 peak, for a 13B-class model on our infra you probably need roughly 2-3 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs to hit steady throughput with low latency. then a burst pool to cover 250 peaks - that's additional 2 GPUs on spot or burst nodes. if you have long sequences (800 tokens) that changes memory + kv cache considerations, might need an extra GPU for prewarm.
[01:20] Anika Patel: hmm 2-3 reserved seems reasonable but cost is a concern, can we trade latency for lower cost?
[01:28] Maya Chen: yep, we usually present options: 1) keep reserved minimal and accept higher p95 on peak, 2) use autoscale with burst (spot) to keep p95 low but add on-demand cost during peaks, or 3) configure fallback policy to use a smaller quantized model for non-critical traffic to reduce GPU pressure.
[01:46] Liam O'Neal: fallback to quantized model — is that seamless? do you do automatic routing?
[01:52] Diego Ramirez: yes we can set routing policies by route/endpoint; for example low priority requests route to a 4-bit quantized variant or to hosted endpoint where cost is absorbed differently. there's some potential quality delta, we should define which prompts can tolerate fallback.
[02:08] Anika Patel: that's important. success criteria for us: p95 < 200ms for core chat flows, <5% request error, and cost target of <$0.50 per 1k requests for the pilot.
[02:20] Maya Chen: noted. Diego, for benchmarking we'll capture p50/p95/p99, throughput, GPU utilization, and tokens/sec cost.
[02:26] Diego Ramirez: exactly. also we'll test warm vs cold starts, impact of KV cache hit rates, and continuous batching config.
[02:34] Priya Singh: what's Redwood's policy on reserved vs dedicated vs private here? we want to understand data residency and KMS.
[02:40] Maya Chen: for POC we usually run on Redwood Dedicated reserved pool in our tenant with VPC peering; KMS integration is supported, logs for audit, and we can discuss Private if you need on-prem later. i'll include SOC2 docs.
[02:52] Liam O'Neal: spot instances for burst — how often do you lose capacity? our concern is for a sudden traffic spike during a release.
[02:58] Diego Ramirez: spot is variable; we recommend a mixed strategy: keep enough reserved capacity for 90-95% day-to-day, burst with spot for short spikes, and have an automatic fallback to lower-cost hosted models or smaller quantized variants if spot eviction occurs. also can configure auto-burst thresholds and cooldowns.
[03:18] Anika Patel: can you give an example config? like thresholds numerically.
[03:22] Diego Ramirez: yes, e.g., reserved pool sized for 80 rps steady; autoscale up when queue latency > 50ms or GPU util > 70% for 30s, add one burst GPU at a time up to 2 GPUs. if burst fails or eviction, route low-priority traffic to quantized model. set cooldown 120s. that's one pattern.
[03:40] Maya Chen: we'll include that in the proposal as a default policy and you can tweak.
[03:45] Liam O'Neal: and for long sequences, how do you handle KV cache memory pressure?
[03:50] Diego Ramirez: we can pin longer-context workloads to nodes with larger memory, and apply prefix caching for repeated prompts. may need to provision an extra GPU or use model sharding for the 800-token flows. we'll test those in bench.
[04:06] Anika Patel: benchmarks — what do you need from us to run them?
[04:10] Maya Chen: 24-48 hour sample traffic trace + 50-100 representative prompts, plus a list of SLA routes and which can tolerate fallback. ideally a synthetic replay so we can do load tests.
[04:20] Anika Patel: okay we'll share that.
[04:24] Diego Ramirez: on benchmarks we'll run p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, cost per token, and end-to-end latency including network overhead. we'll also include a test that simulates spot eviction and see fallback behavior.
[04:38] Priya Singh: security items: KMS, SSO, audit logs retention, and whether logs contain PII.
[04:44] Maya Chen: KMS supported, RBAC + SAML SSO, and audit logging. we can redact PII on ingestion if needed. i'll share security pack.
[04:54] Liam O'Neal: what's the expected timeline?
[04:57] Maya Chen: propose: proposal by 2025-12-05, sample workload by 2025-12-08, benchmark week of 2025-12-08, bench review 2025-12-15, pilot run across 2 weeks, decision by end of Q1.
[05:10] Anika Patel: sounds ok. any questions on cost math?
[05:14] Diego Ramirez: we'll include modeled costs for reserved-only, reserved+spot, and fallback hybrid. include estimated cost per 1k requests given your token distribution.
[05:24] Anika Patel: do you support per-route throttles? we might want to limit certain heavy routes.
[05:30] Maya Chen: yes route-level throttles + quotas and can prioritize by token budget.
[05:34] Liam O'Neal: i'm worried about noise in transcription — sorry, ignore.
[05:37] Diego Ramirez: (laughs) we've all been there.
[10:12] Diego Ramirez: jumping ahead a bit — during bench, we'll also try quantized 4-bit models to compare quality drop vs cost savings. would recommend a small eval set for quality checks so we can measure regressions.
[10:28] Anika Patel: yes we'll provide test prompts and expected outputs or acceptance metrics.
[15:00] Priya Singh: on the networking side, we need VPC peering and static egress IPs for firewall rules. is that something you can accommodate?
[15:10] Maya Chen: yes, we can do VPC peering and provide egress ranges; i'll add that to the infra checklist.
[25:05] Liam O'Neal: what about SLAs for Dedicated during pilot?
[25:12] Maya Chen: pilot doesn't come with full enterprise SLA, but Dedicated reserved pools have SLA options; we can include an SLA addendum for you if needed.
[30:00] Diego Ramirez: one more thing on autoscaling: continuous batching helps improve throughput but can increase tail latency for single request routes; we'll tune batching parameters per-route.
[30:12] Anika Patel: for the success criteria, can you commit to test scenarios and acceptance thresholds?
[30:18] Maya Chen: yes we'll include a test plan: core chat flows measured at p95 <200ms, error rate <5%, fallback quality delta under x% BLEU/ROUGE for summarization (we'll agree on metric), and cost targets.
[45:20] Diego Ramirez: any blockers on Solara side?
[45:24] Anika Patel: infra people need to review the peering and KMS doc; budgeting is the other internal step.
[50:00] Maya Chen: recap then: we'll send capacity/pricing proposal, security pack, and schedule benchmarks. Solara to send sample traffic and prompts. follow-up 2025-12-15 to review.
[50:18] Liam O'Neal: thanks everyone.
[50:20] Priya Singh: thanks, bye.
[50:22] Maya Chen: bye all, will follow up via email with links and the proposal.
questions: Can Redwood support VPC peering and static egress IPs?
How does the burst strategy behave under spot eviction?
What's the expected cost difference between reserved-only and reserved+spot?
How seamless is fallback to quantized models for non-critical traffic?
